# Juicefall

> Juicefall is a falling-jelly puzzle game for iPhone where you match colors, not rows. Free to play, with no ads, no subscription and no account; it collects no data and plays offline. Made by Aaron Seaman. On the App Store as "Juicefall: Jelly Match Puzzle".

How it plays: jelly shapes drop into a garden well; the player slides and turns them. Three or more jellies of one color in a row or a column burst, and whatever falls after a match can match again, so one drop can set off a chain whose every step multiplies the points. Full rows do nothing. Bigger matches make fruit power-ups. Modes: Classic (speeds up every level), Calm (no gravity: shapes fall only when dropped), Hectic (levels up twice as fast), and a daily challenge that is the same puzzle for everyone.

Key facts:

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 26 or later
- Price: free; six fruit power-ups are optional one-time in-app purchases (in the United States US$0.99 or US$1.99 each, or all six for US$5.99); the five games after the first have every fruit for free; Family Sharing included
- Ads: none. Subscription: none. Account: none
- Privacy: App Store privacy label "Data Not Collected"
- Internet: not needed
- Game Center: three leaderboards (Classic, Calm, Hectic) and 27 achievements; records sync through the player's iCloud
- Accessibility: color symbols, Reduce Motion, VoiceOver
- Languages: English, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish
- Age rating: 4+
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823235878
